specification:
# Concise Bounded Description (CBD) for Graph

## Goals
- Add a public method named cbd to the Graph class. Given a resource term, it returns the Concise Bounded Description of that resource from the graph it is called on, as a new in-memory Graph.
- Implement the three CBD rules of the W3C Member Submission (https://www.w3.org/Submission/CBD/) exactly as specified under Workflows. Rule 3 (reification) is part of the required behavior and must not be narrowed.
- Keep the change additive: one method, its docstring, and its tests.

## Scope
In scope: the cbd method on Graph, its docstring, and its tests.

Out of scope:
- Implementing SPARQL DESCRIBE. In this snapshot the SPARQL evaluator raises a "DESCRIBE not implemented" error. This feature does not make DESCRIBE work and must not be described as its prerequisite or building block.
- Adding a formatter, linter, or any other tool to requirements or setup files.
- Changing stores, parsers, serializers, plugins, or the behavior of any existing method, including those on ConjunctiveGraph and Dataset.
- Adding argument validation, argument conversion, or special handling of None.

## Assumptions
- The source graph supports triple-pattern queries in which None is a wildcard for subject, predicate, or object.
- Reification is expressed with rdf:subject triples: a node R is the reified subject of a statement S when S has an rdf:subject triple whose object is R. The rdf:Statement type, rdf:predicate, and rdf:object triples are not needed for a node to count as a reification.

## Terminology
- Starting node: the resource argument passed to cbd.
- Source graph: the Graph on which cbd is called. It is never modified.
- Result: the new Graph returned by cbd.
- Reifier: a node S that has an rdf:subject triple whose object is the node currently being processed.
- Blank node: an rdflib blank node term (the BNode type).

## Workflows
1. Create an empty result Graph.
2. Process the starting node with the node procedure below.

Node procedure (applied to the starting node, and recursively to blank nodes as described in step (a)):
(a) Query the source graph for all triples whose subject is the node. Add each such triple to the result. If a triple's object is a blank node and the result does not already contain any triple whose subject is that blank node, run the node procedure on that blank node. Recursion continues through blank nodes that were not already expanded, so cycles terminate.
(b) After step (a) has finished for this node, query the source graph for all triples whose predicate is rdf:subject and whose object is the node. For each reifier S found, add every triple of the source graph whose subject is S to the result. Include every reifier found, regardless of whether S has an rdf:Statement type, and regardless of whether S's rdf:predicate or rdf:object values match any triple in the source graph.
(c) Do not run the node procedure on blank nodes that are objects of the triples added in step (b). Do not follow the rdf:object or rdf:predicate values of a reifier, and do not follow any triple in which the node appears as an object other than through rdf:subject.
(d) Step (b) runs for every node the procedure processes, including blank nodes reached through step (a). A reifier of a blank node that is part of the description therefore contributes its triples.

Invariants:
- The result contains only triples that exist in the source graph; the source graph is not modified.
- If the starting node has no subject triples and no reifiers, the result is an empty Graph (not an error, not None).
- The result is the set of triples produced by the procedure; the order in which they are added does not matter.

## Data model
- The result is a new default Graph. Namespace bindings from the source graph are not copied.
- The vocabulary terms used are the rdflib RDF namespace's subject term (rdf:subject) and the BNode term type. No new data structures are persisted or exposed.

## API contracts
- cbd is a public method on Graph taking exactly one required positional parameter named resource, with no default and no additional parameters.
- The method returns a new Graph instance. It never returns the source graph itself or a view of it.
- resource is used as given in the triple-pattern queries. The method does not convert it to another term type, does not type-check it, and does not raise for None. Passing None is not special-cased; it passes through as a wildcard, as the reference does.
- Subclasses that inherit cbd (ConjunctiveGraph and Dataset) get the behavior through the triple-pattern query of the instance they are called on, so their context-aware triple queries apply. Do not override cbd in subclasses.

## Module architecture
- The method belongs to the Graph class in the graph module. Place it as the last method of Graph, after the existing Graph methods and before the ConjunctiveGraph class definition.
- Implement the traversal as a helper function nested inside the method. The helper may call itself recursively for blank nodes.
- Responsibility stays in Graph: the method builds on Graph's own triple-pattern query and add operations.

## Implementation constraints
- Read only through Graph's triple-pattern query and write only to the result Graph's add. Do not touch store internals.
- Use the RDF namespace subject term and the BNode type, which are already imported in the graph module. Add no imports.
- Detect blank nodes with an exact type check against the BNode type.
- The cycle guard must match the reference: a blank node is expanded only when the result does not yet contain any triple with that blank node as subject.
- Run step (a) before step (b) for each node, so that the cycle guard sees the triples already added for that node.

## Dependencies
- No new packages, modules, or requirements. The reference changes only the graph module and adds one test file.
- Tests use only rdflib and the standard unittest module.

## Naming
- Method name: cbd. Parameter name: resource. Nested helper name should describe its role (the reference uses a name like add_to_cbd).
- Test file: test/test_graph_cbd.py. Test class: CbdTestCase.
- Test method names use the camelCase testX form used by the repository's Graph tests and by the reference (for example testCbd and testCbdReified).

## Validation
- No input validation is added. Invalid or None arguments are not rejected by cbd.

## Error handling
- cbd raises no exceptions of its own. Missing data yields an empty result Graph.

## Logging
- No logging is added.

## Documentation
- The docstring is the required documentation for cbd. It must follow the repository's Graph docstring style: a summary line, a description of the three CBD rules, a note that the result is a subgraph of the source, and :param resource: and :return: fields.
- The docstring must describe the reification rule as it behaves: every statement whose rdf:subject is the node is included, with no rdf:Statement type check and no predicate or object matching.
- The docstring must not claim that cbd is the basis of SPARQL DESCRIBE, and must not claim W3C conformance for any rule that is not implemented.
- The reference adds no documentation page. Adding one is optional. If a documentation page is added, every RST section underline must be at least as long as its title; "Concise Bounded Description" is 27 characters, so its underline needs at least 27 characters.

## Compatibility
- The change is additive. Existing Graph, ConjunctiveGraph, and Dataset methods keep their current behavior and output.
- cbd is inherited by ConjunctiveGraph and Dataset without any registration.

## Behavioral acceptance criteria
- For a resource with three direct triples, two of which point to URI objects and one of which points to a blank node with a nested blank node, the result contains all triples reachable by rules 1 and 2 (the reference fixture gives 8 for its blank-node resource, 3 for a resource with a type triple and two relation triples, 2 for a resource with two property triples, and 0 for a resource with no triples).
- Reified case A: a resource R5 with three direct triples, plus one typed reifier whose rdf:subject is R5 and which has four other triples (rdf:predicate, rdf:object, and one more property). cbd of R5 returns 8 triples.
- Reified case B: a resource R6 with three direct triples, plus a typed reifier with five triples and an untyped reifier with rdf:subject R6 and four other triples (rdf:predicate, rdf:object, and two more properties). cbd of R6 returns 13 triples. The untyped reifier must be included.
- Incoming reification: when a statement (A p B) exists and a reifier has rdf:subject A and rdf:object B, cbd of B does not include the reifier's triples; cbd of A does.
- A reifier whose triples contain a blank-node object does not cause that blank node's triples to be added, unless the blank node is reached by rules 1 or 2.
- A blank-node cycle terminates and returns each triple once.
- The source graph is unchanged after cbd is called, and the returned object is a different Graph instance.

## Test requirements
- test/test_graph_cbd.py contains a unittest.TestCase class. setUp parses a Turtle fixture and binds the example prefix. tearDown closes the graph.
- Tests must cover: the rules 1 and 2 counts; typed and untyped reifiers (the untyped case must be included); the incoming-reification exclusion; the blank-node-in-reification non-expansion; a blank-node cycle; source-graph immutability.
- Tests must not assert a typed-only reifier rule or a predicate/object matching rule.
- Tests use the repository's existing test runner and add no dependencies.

edits.change: Replaced the PR-author narrative (documentation example, 'not so much a rocket science improvement') with the feature goals: a public Graph.cbd method returning a new in-memory Graph, implementing all three CBD rules, and staying additive.
edits.hypothesis: The old text described the PR rather than the feature, so the implementer had no statement of the required rule 3 behavior. Stating the goal as the full W3C rules addresses the requirement_intent failures in every run.

edits.change: Removed the struck-through note about adding black to requirements.txt.
edits.hypothesis: The reference diff touches only the graph module and a new test file and adds no requirements change. The note conflicts with the reference, so removing it addresses the approved_dependencies and requirement_intent scope.

edits.change: Stated that implementing SPARQL DESCRIBE is out of scope and that cbd must not be described as its building block, because the SPARQL evaluator in this snapshot raises 'DESCRIBE not implemented'.
edits.hypothesis: The original 'precursor to DESCRIBE' claim is false for this snapshot and was repeated in the candidate docs. The clarification addresses the requirement_intent failure caused by the false documentation claim (runs 01, 04, 08).

edits.change: Stated that reification is expressed by rdf:subject triples and that the rdf:Statement type is not required for a node to count as a reification.
edits.hypothesis: Without this, implementers add a typed-only guard. The reference treats any rdf:subject link as a reification, so this addresses the requirement_intent failure where the untyped reifier was dropped (runs 01, 02, 05, 07, 09).

edits.change: Defined starting node, source graph, result, reifier, and blank node. The source graph is stated to be never modified.
edits.hypothesis: Shared terms let the rules in Workflows be applied without ambiguity about which node is processed in rule 3, which was misapplied only to the starting resource in run 03 and run 04.

edits.change: Step (b) of the node procedure: include every reifier S with an rdf:subject triple whose object is the processed node, adding all triples whose subject is S, with no rdf:Statement type check and no predicate or object matching.
edits.hypothesis: The candidate code required rdf:type rdf:Statement and a matching (subject, predicate, object) triple, so it returned 8 triples for the reference's R6 fixture where 13 are expected. The explicit rule removes that guard, addressing the requirement_intent failure in runs 00, 01, 02, 05, 07, 09 and the untyped-reification case.

edits.change: Step (c): do not follow the rdf:object or other values of incoming triples, and do not run the node procedure on blank nodes that are objects of reifier triples.
edits.hypothesis: Run 09 included reifiers whose rdf:object equals the resource (4 triples where the reference gives 0), and runs 01, 07, 08 expanded blank nodes reached through reifications. Limiting traversal to rdf:subject links and not expanding reifier objects matches the reference and addresses the requirement_intent failure.

edits.change: Step (d): the reification step runs for every node the procedure processes, including blank nodes reached in the subject-triple closure, not only for the starting resource.
edits.hypothesis: The reference applies rule 3 to each recursive call. The candidates that applied it only to the starting resource (runs 02, 03) missed reified statements about blank nodes in the closure. Stating the rule addresses that requirement_intent failure.

edits.change: Specified the ordering (subject triples and recursion first, then reifications for each node) and the cycle guard: a blank node is expanded only if the result has no triple with that blank node as subject.
edits.hypothesis: The reference's guard and ordering determine which blank nodes are expanded; leaving them unstated let implementers choose different traversal orders. Pinning them preserves the reference's recursion and termination behavior.

edits.change: Invariants: result contains only source triples; empty Graph for a node with no subject triples and no reifiers; order of addition does not matter.
edits.hypothesis: These states make the empty case (R4 returning 0 triples) and immutability explicit so tests can check them, which addresses the reliability of the reference-pinned counts.

edits.change: The result is a new default Graph with no namespace bindings copied from the source; the terms used are the RDF subject term and the BNode type.
edits.hypothesis: Run 06 and run 07 added namespace copying that the reference does not perform. Specifying the default Graph keeps the output identical to the reference and removes an unrequired divergence.

edits.change: Described the public method as taking exactly one required positional parameter named resource, returning a new Graph, with no conversion, validation, or None special-casing; None passes through as a wildcard, and subclasses ConjunctiveGraph and Dataset inherit the method and must not override it.
edits.hypothesis: Run 03 coerced non-term arguments to URIRef and run 06 treated None as empty, both diverging from the reference's pass-through. Also, cbd depends on the instance's triple query, so overriding it in subclasses would split behavior. This addresses the secondary api_contract divergences noted in runs 03 and 06.

edits.change: Placement: the method is the last method of the Graph class, before the ConjunctiveGraph class; the traversal is a nested helper that may recurse.
edits.hypothesis: Stating the exact placement and helper structure keeps file_location and architectural_fit stable and matches the reference structure.

edits.change: Read only through the triple-pattern query and write only through the result Graph's add; use the already-imported RDF subject term and BNode type with an exact type check; add no imports; the cycle guard and step ordering are fixed as stated in Workflows.
edits.hypothesis: Constraints that fix the query path and the exact type check prevent the parallel or store-level access patterns that the judge checked, and keep the traversal identical to the reference.

edits.change: No new packages, modules, or requirements; tests use only rdflib and the standard unittest module.
edits.hypothesis: States the approved dependency set explicitly, so no formatter or linter dependency is introduced (the approved_dependencies criterion).

edits.change: Specified the method name cbd, parameter resource, test file test/test_graph_cbd.py, class CbdTestCase, and camelCase testX test method names such as testCbd and testCbdReified.
edits.hypothesis: Run 09 used snake_case test names in a camelCase test module, failing convention_fit. Naming the camelCase form and matching the reference addresses that failure.

edits.change: No input validation is added; invalid or None input is not rejected.
edits.hypothesis: States the reference's absence of validation so implementers do not add checks that change the returned graphs for valid inputs.

edits.change: cbd raises no exceptions of its own; missing data yields an empty result Graph.
edits.hypothesis: Makes the empty-result behavior explicit and consistent with the reference's R4 case returning zero triples.

edits.change: The docstring must describe the three rules and the reification behavior as implemented (every statement whose rdf:subject is the node, no type check or predicate/object matching), use :param resource: and :return: fields, and must not claim SPARQL DESCRIBE use or W3C conformance for unimplemented rules. Any new RST section underline must be at least as long as its title; the title 'Concise Bounded Description' needs an underline of at least 27 characters.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 01, 03, 06 produced a 27-character title with a 26-character underline (a Sphinx warning), and runs 02, 03, 06, 08 claimed W3C or DESCRIBE coverage they did not implement. Specifying the underline rule and accurate docstring content addresses the convention_fit and requirement_intent failures.

edits.change: The change is additive; existing Graph, ConjunctiveGraph, and Dataset methods keep their behavior; the method is inherited by subclasses without registration.
edits.hypothesis: Makes explicit that no existing output changes, which the judge checked as no removals in every run, so the constraint is preserved as a compatibility requirement.

edits.change: Replaced the vague reified-case description with concrete expectations: rules 1 and 2 counts (8, 3, 2, 0 in the reference fixture), reified case A returns 8 triples for R5, reified case B returns 13 triples for R6 including an untyped reifier, incoming reifications are excluded, blank-node objects of reifiers are not expanded, cycles terminate, and the source is unchanged.
edits.hypothesis: The judge's failing criterion was the R6 reference count (runs 00, 01, 02, 05, 07, 09 returned 8). Stating the expected counts and the untyped case as acceptance criteria makes the reference behavior testable and addresses requirement_intent.

edits.change: Required test coverage: rules 1 and 2 counts; typed and untyped reifiers; incoming-reification exclusion; blank-node non-expansion under reification; blank-node cycle; source immutability. Tests must not assert a typed-only or predicate/object-matching rule. The setUp parses a Turtle fixture and tearDown closes the graph.
edits.hypothesis: Candidate tests in runs 00, 02, 03, 04, 06, 09 omitted reification or the untyped case and encoded the stricter rule in run 05 and run 07. Required coverage and the prohibition on typed-only assertions address the test-coverage gap behind the requirement_intent failures.
